brief.subject: IRS year-end checklist, Chicago head tax fight, state tax votes
brief.headline: IRS Flags Year-End Steps as Chicago Head Tax and State Tax Measures Advance
brief.dek: The IRS wants taxpayers to act before 2026 ends, Chicago's per-employee tax resurfaces, and wealth-tax measures move in Colorado and California.
brief.lede: The IRS is pressing taxpayers to handle five items before 2026 closes, aiming to smooth the coming filing season and head off April surprises.

sections.heading: IRS Wants Action Before Year-End
bullets: The IRS is recommending five steps now, so start year-end prep early rather than waiting for filing season.
The agency frames these steps as a way to prevent unwelcome surprises at April filing time.
The IRS Advisory Council has scheduled a public meeting, a chance to watch agency priorities take shape.

sections.heading: Chicago Head Tax Back on Table
bullets: Mayor Brandon Johnson is again proposing a per-employee corporate tax in his latest city budget plan.
Gov. JB Pritzker restated his opposition on Thursday, signaling continued state-level resistance.
Chicago employers should track the budget debate, since a head tax would raise payroll-linked costs.

sections.heading: Wealth Tax Fights in Two States
bullets: Colorado's Supreme Court on Friday rejected a bid to void the vote on Amendment 87, a tax hike on top earners.
In California, a billionaire-backed group spent more than $50 million in one week opposing Proposition 40's wealth tax.
High-income owners in both states should watch outcomes that could reshape their personal tax planning.

sections.heading: Film Credit Push in Lame Duck
bullets: A bipartisan coalition is pressing to pass a federal film tax credit before the 119th Congress ends.
Production-related small businesses could benefit if lawmakers act in the remaining weeks.
